key_insight: Token-level credit in long-CoT RLVR is highly uneven: large likelihood shifts mostly reflect counterfactual sensitivity of surface-form tokens, not reliable answer-aligned learning signals.
engineering_relevance: For reasoning-model training, CSCR improves upon uniform token credit assignment in GRPO by downweighting sensitive tokens while preserving verifier-determined update direction and total credit budget.
method: Re-score each sampled trajectory under two opposite outcomes: correct vs incorrect.
Measure token sensitivity from the induced likelihood shifts and reduce credit for highly sensitive tokens.
Renormalize token advantages so the original credit budget and RL signal direction are preserved.
evidence_signal: The authors test fixed trajectories under opposing outcome conditions and evaluate CSCR on long-CoT mathematical reasoning benchmarks, where it consistently outperforms GRPO with the same number of policy updates.
watch_item: Over-downweighting sensitive tokens can destabilize optimization, so the credit modulation strength needs careful tuning.
paper_title: Not All Tokens Deserve Equal Credit: Counterfactual Sensitivity Credit Reallocation for Long-CoT Reasoning
